comparator.name: Communicatie- en informatiewetenschappen
comparator.academicYear: Adopted OER 2026–27 for students starting in 2026; checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 OER establishes a 120-EC major and 60-EC profiling space. The major comprises eight compulsory 7.5-EC foundation courses (60 EC), Schrijven, redeneren & presenteren and Informatiekunde (15 EC), one compulsory-choice 30-EC deepening package, CIW-Lab (7.5 EC) and the BA-eindwerkstuk (7.5 EC). Four formal deepening packages are listed. Because the normalized target names no package, the first-listed package, Media, data en maatschappij, is selected independently of UCR fit under the official-order tiebreak. The 60-EC profiling space remains open, including the requirement for a coherent 30-EC profiling package.

routeSelection.basis: The target names the ordinary CIW bachelor but no deepening package. The adopted OER lists four equal-status compulsory-choice packages and places Media, data en maatschappij first. It is therefore selected neutrally from official order, not because of similarity to UCR; the 60-EC profiling space remains genuinely open.

core: Communication and media theory across language, image, audiovisual and digital forms
Meaning, rhetoric, persuasion, interaction and effective message design
Media technologies, platforms, institutions and their social, political and cultural contexts
Communication research, qualitative and quantitative methods, digital data and AI literacy
Professional and organisational communication, advice and improvement
Critical and ethical analysis of representation, identity, diversity and media power
adjacent: Cognition, emotion, psychology and audience response
Media industries, advertising, markets and creator economies
questions: How do messages, language and images influence people?
How do digital platforms and algorithms shape information and participation?
How can communication processes in organisations and society be analysed and improved?

candidates.label: Culture, communication and diversity
candidates.reason: This is a formally supported fourth package, but the three-alternative production maximum has been reached. Its culture, identity, diversity and representation content remains visible within the included media and organisational alternatives.

alternatives.label: Media, data and society
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule mirrors the neutrally selected formal package through media theory, digital platforms, visual and data methods, algorithms, society, representation and advanced communication research.
alternatives.concept: A communication and media programme focused on digital platforms, data, algorithms and their social consequences, while retaining rhetoric, language, visual analysis, qualitative research, representation and ethics.
progression: Introductory communication, film/media and brain-and-behaviour work precedes advanced persuasion, media, psycholinguistics and research courses. Qualitative and introductory data methods precede advanced platform, algorithmic and research applications. Every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Media, communication and markets
alternatives.labelReason: This formal package is represented by media analysis combined with economics, marketing, consumer engagement, product design, digital strategy, market research and leadership communication.
alternatives.concept: A media and communication programme centred on media industries, audiences, advertising, markets and organisational strategy, supported by rhetorical, qualitative and creative methods.
progression: Business and research-method gateways precede advanced marketing, strategy, organisational leadership and market research. Introductory rhetoric and media courses precede advanced persuasive, creative, representational and documentary work. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the media-data closest match, this route replaces brain-and-behaviour, image processing, data science, media-and-environment, databases, machine learning, social theory, psycholinguistics, advanced psychology research and ethics with business foundations, economics, marketing, digital strategy, consumer-product design, organisational leadership, market research, diversity management and leadership communication.

alternatives.label: Communication, organisation and interaction
alternatives.labelReason: This formal package is represented by rhetoric, persuasive and creative communication, social and organisational psychology, leadership, qualitative and experimental methods, and interaction across organisational settings.
alternatives.concept: A communication programme focused on interpersonal influence, cognition, organisational culture, leadership and interaction, with qualitative, statistical and advanced research preparation.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, business, psychology and research-method foundations precede advanced persuasive communication, organisational leadership, psycholinguistics and psychology research. Rhetoric develops from introduction through applied and advanced creative work. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the media-data closest match, this route replaces eight media/data courses plus political philosophy, ethics and media-and-environment with business foundations, social and experimental psychology, research statistics, organisational leadership, sociology, abnormal and health psychology, diversity management and lifespan psychology. The completed programme therefore centres human and organisational interaction rather than digital-platform analysis.

blocks: Both introduce frameworks for analysing communication and its effects.
Both examine how formal choices in messages produce meaning; UCR concentrates on linguistic style.
Both analyse communication in interaction; UCR approaches it through applied rhetoric.
Both examine influence and the design of more effective messages.
Both connect language and communication to cognitive or technological systems, while the comparator gives greater emphasis to generative AI and societal implications.
The comparator's dedicated academic writing, reasoning and presentation course has no sufficiently direct single UCR counterpart.
Both introduce media institutions, forms and their relationship with society.
Both examine how media technologies develop and reshape communication, though UCR is more historically oriented.
Both study platform-era media production, creators and audience participation.
The integrated comparator component combines mediatisation, datafication, social platforms and critical issues; no unused single UCR course adequately represents that full primary focus.
Both develop empirical research design, data collection, analysis and interpretation; UCR emphasises qualitative methodology.
Both prepare students to design and execute advanced research; the comparator lab directly develops the thesis proposal.
Both analyse visual information and how formal image features shape interpretation, with UCR using computational image methods.
Both develop foundational understanding of information and its organisation; UCR is more data-analytic.
Both use computational methods and AI critically in research; the comparator focuses on digital media and society.
The comparator requires a 7.5-EC independent research project; UCR's standardized optional independent research element is displayed alongside it.
The comparator's 60-EC profiling space remains open, including its coherent 30-EC package requirement.

selection.assessment: The closest match represents the neutrally selected Media, data en maatschappij package. Two further formal packages support coherent, substantially distinct UCR alternatives in media markets and organisational interaction. The fourth formal package, culture and diversity, remains academically defensible but is excluded by the maximum of three alternatives; its subject matter is still represented across included courses.

notes.text: Utrecht CIW combines a prescribed communication core, one coherent 30-EC deepening package, a dedicated CIW research lab and compulsory bachelor thesis with 60 EC of profiling space. UCR can build strong media-data, media-market and organisational-communication programmes, but it does not reproduce each Utrecht package course-for-course or require an equivalent CIW thesis; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.
